content.user_title: Build Modern Android Interfaces with Jetpack Compose
content.value_statement: Complex Compose applications require consistent patterns for state, navigation, and recomposition. This skill provides focused Kotlin guidance and production-oriented examples for modern Android interfaces.
actual_capabilities: Recommends Compose dependencies through a Gradle version catalog and BOM.
Demonstrates ViewModel state exposure with StateFlow and lifecycle-aware collection.
Separates screen-level state handling from stateless UI components.
Shows type-safe Navigation Compose destinations and route arguments.
Identifies common recomposition problems and practical performance patterns.
limitations: Dependency versions are examples and may require updates for the target project.
The guidance does not inspect, compile, or test an Android project automatically.
Examples omit complete imports, repository implementations, and dependency injection setup.
Project-specific architecture, accessibility, and device behavior still require validation.

use_cases.title: Start a Compose Application
use_cases.description: Define dependencies, state ownership, and screen structure for a new Android application.
use_cases.target_user: Android developers starting a Compose project

use_cases.title: Migrate Legacy Screens
use_cases.description: Plan how XML screens can become state-driven Composable screens with clear component boundaries.

use_cases.title: Review Compose Performance
use_cases.description: Find unstable state, unnecessary recomposition, and expensive work inside Composable functions.
use_cases.target_user: Senior engineers reviewing production UI code

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Screen
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Jetpack Compose screen for [feature] with loading, content, and error states.
prompt_templates.scenario: A beginner needs a clear screen structure.

prompt_templates.title: Model Screen State
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a ViewModel and immutable UI state for [feature] using StateFlow and lifecycle-aware collection.
prompt_templates.scenario: An application needs predictable state management.

prompt_templates.title: Add Type-Safe Navigation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design type-safe Navigation Compose routes for [screens], including [arguments] and callback-based child components.
prompt_templates.scenario: A multi-screen application needs safer routing.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose Recomposition
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this Compose design for unstable parameters, unnecessary recomposition, side-effect errors, and expensive work: [design description].
prompt_templates.scenario: An advanced developer is investigating UI performance.

output_examples.input: Design state handling for a user profile screen.
output: Use one immutable profile state with loading, user, and error values.
Expose a read-only StateFlow from the ViewModel.
Collect state with lifecycle awareness at the screen boundary.
Pass state and event callbacks to a stateless profile component.

output_examples.input: How should profile navigation carry a user identifier?
output_examples.output: Define a serializable profile destination with a user identifier. Navigate with the typed destination and recover it from the back stack entry.

output_examples.input: Why does my list recompose too often?
output_examples.output: Check for new collections or modifiers created during composition. Stabilize UI state and remember derived calculations before measuring recomposition again.

best_practices: Keep mutable state private and expose read-only StateFlow values.
Pass data and event callbacks to child Composables instead of ViewModel instances.
Measure recomposition after stabilizing parameters and remembering derived calculations.
anti_patterns: Do not update state directly during the composition phase.
Do not perform sorting or other expensive work in a Composable body.
Do not assume example dependency versions match every project.

faq.question: Does this skill generate a complete Android project?
faq.answer: No. It provides patterns and examples that must be integrated into an existing or new project.

faq.question: Does it support XML layouts?
faq.answer: It focuses on Jetpack Compose, but its state and migration guidance can help replace XML-based screens.

faq.question: Which architecture does it recommend?
faq.answer: It demonstrates MVVM or MVI-style state flow with a ViewModel, immutable UI state, and stateless child components.

faq.question: Can it help with navigation arguments?
faq.answer: Yes. It demonstrates serializable destinations, typed navigation calls, and typed route recovery.

faq.question: Can it diagnose performance without project data?
faq.answer: It can identify likely causes, but accurate diagnosis requires code context and recomposition measurements.

faq.question: Are the dependency versions current?
faq.answer: They are illustrative versions from the skill content. Verify compatible stable releases before implementation.
